hook_text: There is a way to know, in ten seconds, whether the fish on your plate is helping the ocean or harming it.
clip_script: The ocean is not endless. More than a third of the world's fish stocks are over-fished. So how do we keep fish in the sea? First, science. Count the fish, then set a limit on how many can be caught. Second, rules. No fishing in the breeding season. Throw back fish that are too small. Third, nurseries. Marine protected areas, where fish grow big and spill out into the sea around them. South Africa's hake was managed this way, and in 2004 it became the first hake fishery in the world certified sustainable. And fourth, you. SASSI works like a traffic light. Green: go for it. Orange: think twice. Red: stop, it's illegal. Type the name of a fish into your phone, and you'll know in seconds.
visual_style: A fish shop counter with green, orange and red labels; scientists measuring fish on a research boat; a net with large mesh letting small fish escape; divers among big fish in Tsitsikamma; a trawler with a certified ecolabel; a teenager checking a phone in a restaurant.
pacing: Clear, punchy steps, ending with the call to the viewer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how fishing can be made sustainable.
